key_insight: Environment-aware divide-and-conquer compilation improves MPS state-preparation accuracy over unitary-distance-based compilation while preserving task-level parallelism.
engineering_relevance: Choosing compilation methods by system size, MPS bond dimension, and target infidelity can improve resource efficiency when preparing strongly correlated molecular states.
method: Benchmark analytical, variational, and hybrid MPS-to-circuit compilation methods.
Optimize local isometry approximations according to their contribution to prepared-state fidelity.
Combine environment-aware compilation with entanglement-minimized orbitals for FeMoco.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on hydrogen chains and iron–sulfur clusters compare infidelity, CNOT count, classical runtime, and parallel scalability, finding complementary regimes for variational and divide-and-conquer methods.
watch_item: No single method dominates: resource efficiency depends on system size, bond dimension, orbital choice, and accuracy target.
paper_title: Initial-State Preparation for Strongly Correlated Molecules from Matrix Product States: Benchmarking and Environment-Aware Divide-and-Conquer Compilation
